### Detecting the legacy of deep-time environmental dynamics in the diversification of clades

The idea that clade macroevolutionary dynamics are influenced by environmental changes -- encompassing both biotic and abiotic factors [*e*.*g*., @barnosky2001] -- has been central to this doctoral work. As detailed in the \textcolor{Blue}{General Introduction}, testing the hypotheses relating clade diversification dynamics to environmental changes yielded substantial methodological improvements in the field of macroevolution [*e*.*g*., @condamine2013; @lehtonen2017; @palazzesi2022]. That being said, the philosophy behind nay model-based approach has always been to chose the 'least worst' model  following a given criterion (*e*.*g*., likelihood-based approaches)

It is easy to draw biologically-irrelevant correlations, hence the importance of having clearly defined hypotheses prior any analysis.

Avenue: mechanistic modelling. Can be Mechanistic Eco-Evolutionary Simulations, but also causal inference, such as structural equation models or phylogenetic path analyses.

The uncertainty may never be solved. However, one approach to resolve it lies in combining several approaches [*e*.*g*., @toussaint2025]. That's what we intended to do with MBD/BDNN in \textcolor{Blue}{Chapter 2}.

Phylogenies are the big absent
